name: AI power and the grid
thesis: AI data centers have turned flat US power demand into a growth market, and the binding constraint is now physical equipment, not chips: gas turbines are sold out for years, large transformers take three to four years, and PJM capacity auctions are clearing at the price cap. The best risk/reward sits with suppliers of scarce long lead hardware (turbines, transformers, switchgear, HV cable, grain oriented steel) and with owners of existing firm generation (nuclear and gas) that can sign long term contracts with hyperscalers. Speed to power is creating a parallel behind the meter market (fuel cells, aeroderivative and reciprocating engines, batteries) that bypasses slow grid interconnection. Nuclear is a slower, policy backed second wave (Westinghouse AP1000 program, SMRs, HALEU enrichment) where fuel supply is the chokepoint. The main risk is an AI capex pause that strands orders placed at peak lead times.

facts: GE Vernova gas power backlog plus slot reservation agreements reached 116 GW at end of Q2 2026, up from 100 GW three months earlier (Q2 2026 results, July 2026).
In Q2 2026 GE Vernova signed 20 GW of new gas equipment contracts (18 GW slot reservations, 2 GW orders); backlog rose from 44 to 53 GW and slot reservations from 56 to 63 GW.
GE Vernova raised its target to at least 125 GW of gas equipment under contract by end of 2026, from a prior 110 GW goal.
Total GE Vernova backlog was reported at about $176 billion (pulse2 summary of 2026 results).

pipeline.timing: Next auction cycle (date per PJM schedule, unverified)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: The 2027/2028 auction cleared at the $333.44/MW-day cap and came in 6,623 MW short of the reliability requirement. Another capped, short auction keeps pressure on states and utilities to fast track new gas and storage, which supports turbine, transformer and battery orders.

pipeline.product: GE Vernova and Siemens Energy quarterly order updates
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Conversion of slot reservations into firm orders is the cleanest read on whether data center demand is real money. Siemens Energy backlog was about 69 GW in its fiscal Q3 2026 with lead times of three years or more.

pipeline.product: Westinghouse AP1000 fleet under the $80 billion US government partnership
pipeline.timing: Announced October 2025; long lead item financing and site selection 2026 to 2027
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Large forgings, reactor components, nuclear grade valves and pumps, and fuel fabrication see multi year demand. Beneficiaries include Cameco and Brookfield (owners), BWXT, Curtiss-Wright and enrichment suppliers.

pipeline.product: Centrus HALEU cascade expansion under $900 million DOE task order
pipeline.timing: Contract finalized 2026; 1 metric ton HALEU delivery required by March 2032
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Gives advanced reactor developers (Oklo, X-energy, TerraPower) a domestic fuel path. Centrifuge manufacturing and Piketon construction ramp.

pipeline.timing: Under construction; NRC approved principal design criteria topical report in 2026
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: First commercial advanced fission unit would validate the SMR supply chain and HALEU demand. Delays would hit the speculative SMR names hardest.

pipeline.product: Bloom Energy deliveries to Oracle and AEP
pipeline.timing: Through 2026 and 2027; Oracle agreement up to 2.8 GW with 1.2 GW firm as of April 2026
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Validates behind the meter fuel cells as primary power. Raises natural gas pipeline laterals and on site gas supply demand.
New domestic transformer capacity arrives late in the decade, so pricing power for incumbents likely persists through 2028.

pipeline.product: Blue Energy gas plus nuclear plant at the Port of Victoria, Texas (GE Vernova turbines, GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 reactors)
pipeline.timing: ERCOT connection requests filed (reported Oct 7, 2026); about 1 GW of gas with units expected in 2030 and 2031, then up to five BWRX-300s (up to 1.5 GW); final investment decision targeted for 2027
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: A data center campus is ordering gas turbines now to bridge to small reactors later, which adds to GE Vernova's turbine queue and gives its SMR design another US site. Dates are targets, not commitments.

layers.name: Fuel: natural gas and pipelines
layers.why: Gas is the fastest firm power at scale, both for utility plants and for behind the meter campuses, so data center load turns into incremental gas demand and pipeline lateral projects.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Gas supply is ample, but pipeline permitting and takeaway capacity in some regions are slow.

companies.name: Williams Companies
companies.role: Interstate pipelines (Transco) and dedicated behind the meter power projects for data centers
companies.note: Pipeline owner with data center power projects; check latest project list.

companies.name: Kinder Morgan
companies.role: Largest US gas pipeline network, Texas and Southeast supply to power plants
companies.note: Benefits from gas fired generation buildout volume.

companies.name: EQT Corporation
companies.role: Largest US gas producer, Appalachia supply near PJM data center clusters
companies.note: Commodity price exposure; options sellers should note gas volatility.

layers.name: Gas turbines and engines
layers.why: Large frame turbines are the primary new firm capacity for the grid and big campuses, and they are sold out into the 2028 to 2031 window.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Wood Mackenzie estimates about 110 GW of global turbine orders against 60 to 70 GW of annual manufacturing throughput; OEM lead times are reported at five to seven years for new units, and Mitsubishi deliveries are scheduled 2028 to 2030.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.role: Largest heavy duty gas turbine maker; also grid equipment and wind
companies.note: 116 GW gas backlog plus slot reservations at Q2 2026. Two 7HA.02 turbines are planned for Blue Energy's Texas gas plus nuclear plant, which filed for ERCOT connection (reported Oct 7, 2026).

companies.name: Siemens Energy
companies.role: Number two gas turbine maker; grid technologies
companies.note: US OTC ADR SMNEY. Gas turbine backlog about 69 GW in fiscal Q3 2026.

companies.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
companies.role: Number three large frame gas turbine maker
companies.note: US OTC MHVYF. Large frame backlog about 35 GW; doubling capacity from 2024 level.

companies.name: Caterpillar
companies.role: Solar Turbines industrial turbines and reciprocating gensets for backup and prime power
companies.note: Power generation is one segment of a diversified company.

companies.name: Cummins
companies.role: Backup diesel and gas generator sets for data centers
companies.note: Data center backup gensets are a growth line inside a truck engine company.

companies.name: Baker Hughes
companies.role: Aeroderivative and NovaLT turbines for on site and pipeline power
companies.note: Reported a record quarter for gas turbine orders alongside GEV and Siemens Energy (Turbomachinery, Aug 2026).

companies.name: Wartsila
companies.role: Medium speed gas engines for flexible and behind the meter plants
companies.note: US OTC WRTBY.

layers.name: Behind the meter generation, fuel cells and storage
layers.why: Hyperscalers want power in months, not the years needed for grid interconnection, so on site fuel cells, engines and batteries fill the gap.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Fuel cell and battery factories can scale faster than turbines, but financing and gas hookups gate deployments.

companies.name: Bloom Energy
companies.role: Solid oxide fuel cells as primary on site power
companies.note: Up to 2.8 GW to Oracle (1.2 GW firm as of April 2026), $2.65 billion AEP supply deal, Brookfield financing expanded to $25 billion in June 2026. Risk: on Sep 24, 2026 Oracle sent a force majeure notice on Project Jupiter (New Mexico, designed for up to 2.45 GW of Bloom fuel cells) after its gas pipeline slipped to Feb 1, 2027; Oracle says the project is on schedule.

companies.name: Fluence Energy
companies.role: Utility scale and data center battery storage systems
companies.note: Record $6.4 billion backlog; about $850 million of data center business through July 2026 including about $550 million from one hyperscaler.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.role: Megapack battery storage
companies.note: 46.7 GWh storage deployed in 2025, a record; storage is a small part of Tesla value.

companies.name: Generac
companies.role: Backup generators, entering large data center gensets
companies.note: Mostly residential today; data center line is an option.

layers.name: Nuclear fuel: uranium mining, conversion and enrichment
layers.why: Existing reactors are being life extended and uprated and new reactors need fuel, while Russian enrichment is being phased out of US supply.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Western enrichment and conversion capacity is thin; Centrus is the only US facility producing HALEU as of May 2026. Primary uranium supply is concentrated in Kazakhstan and Canada.

companies.name: Cameco
companies.role: Uranium mining, conversion, fuel services; 49% owner of Westinghouse
companies.note: 2026 production outlook 19.5 to 21.5 million lb; Q2 2026 average realized uranium price about $78.50/lb.

companies.name: Kazatomprom
companies.role: Largest uranium producer globally
companies.note: London GDR; not easily traded in US accounts.

companies.name: Centrus Energy
companies.role: Only US HALEU producer; LEU trading; centrifuge enrichment
companies.note: $900 million DOE HALEU task order (total value up to $1.07 billion); HALEU supply deal with Oklo from 2029.

companies.name: Uranium Energy Corp
companies.role: US in situ uranium producer and conversion ambitions
companies.note: Higher beta uranium equity.

companies.name: Energy Fuels
companies.role: US uranium producer at White Mesa mill; also rare earths
companies.note: Overlaps with critical materials theme.

companies.name: NexGen Energy
companies.role: Developer of Rook I (Arrow) uranium project in Saskatchewan
companies.note: Development stage.

companies.name: Sprott Physical Uranium Trust
companies.role: Physical uranium holding vehicle
companies.note: Primary listing U.UN on TSX; OTC in US. Spot price proxy.

layers.name: Reactors, SMRs and nuclear components
layers.why: Firm carbon free power is what hyperscalers most want for long term contracts, and the US government is financing a large reactor program.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Large forgings, qualified nuclear suppliers, NRC licensing and skilled labor are all scarce; SMRs remain pre revenue.

companies.name: BWX Technologies
companies.role: Naval reactors, nuclear components, fuel and isotopes
companies.note: Sole supplier of naval nuclear reactors; overlaps with defense theme.

companies.name: Curtiss-Wright
companies.role: Reactor coolant pumps and nuclear valves (AP1000 supplier)
companies.note: Key AP1000 component supplier.

companies.name: Oklo
companies.role: Advanced fast reactor (Aurora) developer
companies.note: Pre revenue; NRC approved principal design criteria report in 2026. Very high implied volatility.

companies.name: NuScale Power
companies.role: Only NRC design approved SMR; TVA and ENTRA1 6 GW agreement
companies.note: ENTRA1 would finance and own plants and sell output to TVA.

companies.name: Fluor
companies.role: EPC contractor and large NuScale shareholder
companies.note: Has been monetizing NuScale stake (unverified current size).

companies.name: Brookfield Corporation
companies.role: Co owner of Westinghouse via Brookfield entities; financing partner for Bloom
companies.note: Westinghouse owned with Cameco; US government gets 20% of cash distributions above $17.5 billion once vested.

layers.name: Grid equipment: transformers, switchgear, electrical steel
layers.why: Every new plant and data center needs step up transformers, substations and switchgear, and these were already short before AI.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Generator step up transformer lead times passed 160 weeks in Q1 2026; Wood Mackenzie estimates a 15% power transformer shortage in 2026. Grain oriented electrical steel has one US producer.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.role: Switchgear, UPS, power distribution for data centers and utilities
companies.note: Broad electrical franchise.

companies.name: Hubbell
companies.role: Utility transmission and distribution components
companies.note: Utility capex beneficiary.

companies.name: Powell Industries
companies.role: Custom switchgear and electrical houses
companies.note: Small cap, oil and gas plus utility and data center end markets.

companies.name: Hitachi (Hitachi Energy)
companies.role: Large power transformers, HVDC
companies.note: US OTC HTHIY. About $1.5 billion US manufacturing program including a $528 million Mississippi transformer plant producing from 2029.

companies.name: Schneider Electric
companies.role: Switchgear, data center power and cooling
companies.note: US OTC SBGSY. Agreed Oct 5, 2026 to buy PTC for $205 a share in cash (about $23.7B EV, up to EUR 17B of new debt); shares fell about 10% that day.

companies.name: ABB
companies.role: Electrification, switchgear, drives
companies.note: US OTC ABBNY.

companies.name: Cleveland-Cliffs
companies.role: Only US producer of grain oriented electrical steel (GOES) for transformers
companies.note: GOES is small vs Cliffs auto steel business, but it is the upstream chokepoint for US transformers.

layers.name: Data center power and cooling
layers.why: Inside the fence, every megawatt of IT load needs UPS, power distribution and liquid cooling, which scales with AI rack density.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Capacity is being added quickly, but high density liquid cooling and 800 V power architectures are new and supplier qualified.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.role: Data center power, thermal management and liquid cooling
companies.note: Most direct listed play on data center electrical and thermal content.

layers.name: HV cable and transmission construction
layers.why: New generation and data center clusters need high voltage lines and interconnects, and contractors and cable plants are booked out.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Prysmian transmission backlog fills capacity almost fully until 2028; skilled line workers are scarce.

companies.name: Prysmian
companies.role: Largest cable maker; HV and HVDC cable, US data center cabling
companies.note: US OTC PRYMY. Transmission backlog about EUR 17 billion; $1.25 billion US expansion.

companies.name: Nexans
companies.role: HV subsea and land cable
companies.note: Limited US access (thin OTC).

companies.name: Quanta Services
companies.role: Largest US grid and transmission contractor
companies.note: Record backlog of $53.4 billion at Q2 2026.

companies.name: MasTec
companies.role: Transmission, pipeline and power plant construction
companies.note: Also benefits from gas pipeline work.

companies.name: Comfort Systems USA
companies.role: Mechanical and electrical contractor for data centers
companies.note: Record backlog $14.1 billion at Q2 2026, up 73% year over year.

companies.name: EMCOR Group
companies.role: Electrical and mechanical construction for data centers and fabs
companies.note: Overlaps with reshoring theme.

layers.name: Utilities and independent power producers with data center deals
layers.why: Owners of existing firm generation can sign long dated contracts with hyperscalers at premium prices, and regulated utilities grow rate base to serve new load.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Existing nuclear and gas plants are scarce assets, but regulatory pushback on co location and ratepayer cost shifting is a real constraint.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.role: Largest US nuclear fleet; Meta Clinton 20 year PPA from 2027
companies.note: Clinton is 1,092 MW; Meta deal announced June 2025. Oct 6, 2026: 20 year PPA with Google for 890 MW of new nuclear output from uprates at 11 existing units (first online 2028), plus a 15 year supply deal for another 2,700 MW in PJM, backed by $4.3 billion of investment.

companies.name: Vistra
companies.role: Nuclear and gas IPP; Comanche Peak power to Amazon
companies.note: 20 year PPA with Amazon from Comanche Peak, deliveries starting 2027 (1.2 GW deal per Utility Dive).

companies.name: Talen Energy
companies.role: Susquehanna nuclear; AWS PPA up to 1,920 MW through 2042
companies.note: Full volume ramp no later than 2032.

companies.name: NRG Energy
companies.role: Texas and PJM IPP with data center supply contracts
companies.note: 445 MW of long term data center contracts across ERCOT and PJM; bought 18 GW from LS Power.

companies.name: American Electric Power
companies.role: Regulated utility in PJM and ERCOT; Bloom fuel cell buyer
companies.note: Large rate base growth from data center load.

companies.name: Dominion Energy
companies.role: Serves Northern Virginia, the largest data center market
companies.note: Regulated; ratepayer politics risk.

companies.name: Entergy
companies.role: Gulf South utility serving large new data center campuses
companies.note: Serves Meta Louisiana campus (unverified current size).

companies.name: Southern Company
companies.role: Georgia Power, large data center load pipeline, Vogtle AP1000 owner
companies.note: Only US utility to have completed AP1000s.

companies.name: DTE Energy
companies.role: Michigan utility; contracts to power Google's 1 GW Van Buren Township data center
companies.note: Michigan PSC gave conditional approval (early Oct 2026): 20 year contract, minimum bill of 80% of contracted capacity, and a termination payment covering at least 15 years of minimum charges.

companies.name: WEC Energy Group
companies.role: We Energies; Point Beach nuclear subscription for Oracle's Port Washington AI campus
companies.note: Oct 2, 2026: Oracle to subscribe to 10% to 20% of Point Beach output (125 to 250 MW) for a campus of close to 1 GW of AI capacity.

second_order.idea: Grain oriented electrical steel scarcity favors the one US producer and transformer makers with captive steel
second_order.why: Transformer shortage traces upstream to GOES supply; a US executive order restricting Chinese bulk power equipment worsens the gap per Wood Mackenzie.

second_order.idea: Gas producers and pipelines as the quiet beneficiaries of turbine and fuel cell buildout
second_order.why: Every gas turbine and Bloom fuel cell adds firm gas burn for decades.

second_order.idea: Electrical and mechanical contractors capture labor scarcity rents
second_order.why: Backlogs at FIX ($14.1 billion) and PWR ($53.4 billion) are records; labor, not equipment, gates on site work.

second_order.idea: Copper demand from grid and data centers
second_order.why: Transmission, transformers and data center busbars are copper intensive; see critical materials theme.

second_order.idea: Nuclear fuel enrichment as the narrowest pipe in the nuclear chain
second_order.why: Reactors can be built over a decade, but fuel must be contracted now; HALEU has one US producer.

risks.risk: Hyperscaler capex slowdown or AI model efficiency gains cut power forecasts
risks.signal: Hyperscaler capex guidance cuts; slot reservations at GEV not converting to orders; data center lease cancellations.

risks.risk: Regulators block or reprice co location and shift costs to data centers
risks.signal: FERC rulings on co location; state large load tariffs; PJM market reform proposals.

risks.risk: Turbine and transformer capacity additions overshoot by 2029 to 2030
risks.signal: Lead times shortening; price escalation clauses removed; Mitsubishi and Siemens capacity doubling coming online.

risks.risk: SMR delays, cost overruns or NRC setbacks
risks.signal: Missed construction milestones at Oklo Idaho; ENTRA1 financing not closing.

risks.risk: Natural gas price spike raises power costs and political backlash
risks.signal: Henry Hub forward curve; LNG export growth; state utility commission rate case denials.

changes.what: Constellation signed a 20 year deal with Google for 890 MW of new nuclear output from uprates at 11 existing reactors, plus a 15 year supply deal for another 2,700 MW in PJM. Owners of existing nuclear plants keep getting paid first for firm power.

Oracle sent a force majeure notice on Project Jupiter, a site designed for up to 2.45 GW of Bloom fuel cells, after its gas pipeline slipped to Feb 1, 2027; Oracle says the project is on schedule. Separately, Blue Energy filed to connect a Texas gas plus nuclear plant to ERCOT, starting with about 1 GW of GE Vernova turbines. On site power still depends on gas hookups, and turbine orders keep landing at GE Vernova.
